title: Transfer Swift toolchain selection ownership from Vaporize to Temper

verification: swift package dump-package succeeded from canonical Vaporize on Windows.
swift build succeeded from canonical Vaporize on Windows.
The complete Vaporize test graph compiled while running the focused suite.
Active Package.swift, sources, and tests contain no Swiftly dependency or VAPORIZE_DISABLE_SWIFTLY flag.
Active sources and tests contain no direct Foundation Process or Pipe construction. Test subprocesses use CommonProcess through VaporizeTestCommand.
delivery.ownershipBoundary: Temper owns Swift toolchain selection and lifecycle. Vaporize consumes the selected swift from PATH and retains only its macOS xcode-select provider.

description: Vaporize still embeds Swiftly's command surface and proxy behavior even though Temper now owns Swift toolchain specialization. This duplicates ownership and couples Vaporize builds to an unrelated lifecycle dependency.

historicalContent.expectedBehavior: Vaporize executes builds with the already selected swift on PATH and retains only its macOS-specific xcode-select lane. Temper owns Swift toolchain selection and lifecycle.
currentEvidence: Package.swift conditionally adds swiftlang/swiftly and SwiftlyCommands.
VaporizeExecutable dispatches non-canonical executable names through SwiftlyProxy.
toolchain-selection swift compiles SwiftlyCommandRunner into the Vaporize CLI.
VAPORIZE_DISABLE_SWIFTLY exists solely to make source builds work without that optional graph.
acceptanceCriteria: Remove the Swiftly package and target dependencies from Vaporize.
Remove Swiftly proxy dispatch and toolchain-selection swift from the public command surface.
Remove VAPORIZE_DISABLE_SWIFTLY from active build and test paths.
Retain selected-swift execution through PATH and macOS-only xcode-select behavior.
Update active CUJs and product documentation to identify Temper as the Swift toolchain owner.
Build and run focused tests successfully from canonical Vaporize on Windows.
historicalContent.scopeBoundary: Historical receipts and incident records remain immutable evidence; this refactor changes active code, tests, manifests, and current product documentation only.
